newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Daewoo to invest $1.25 billion in Uzbek telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo to invest $1.25 billion in Uzbek telecoms.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Group will invest around $1.25 billion in the Central Asian nation of Uzbekistan's telecommunications sector by 2010, a senior Daewoo executive said on Wednesday.
Part of a major project to modernise regional telecommunications has already been signed with the Uzbek government, Daewoo Project Manager Kyoung-Mun Shin told Reuters in the Uzbek capital Tashkent.
He said the company has received a licence from the Uzbek telecommunications ministry to provide digital mobile telephone and paging services across the republic of 22 million.
Uzbek officials were not immediately available for comment.

Investment for the mobile telephone service for 300,000 subscribers and a paging service for 500,000 subscribers will total $450 million, he said. He said the investment would comprise 100 percent foreign capital.

Kyoung-Mun said the largest project, worth $800 million, will be a joint venture with state-owned Uzbektelekom to modernise telecommunications in five regions -- Tashkent, Fergana, Andijan, Namangan and Syrdarya.
The joint-venture, to be 49 percent-owned by Daewoo, has already been established for the Fergana and Andijan regions, he said.
Uzbekistan's Soviet-era telephone system makes placing calls simply across town in the capital Tashkent a challenge.

An international tender announced earlier this month remains open to modernise other spheres in Uzbek telecommunications using a 12.7 billion yen credit from Japan's Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund. The tender closes September 23.
